brief: For the first time since the Iran conflict began, J.P. Morgan says it has no baseline view for how it ends. Assumed US red lines ($100 oil, $5 gasoline, 4% inflation, a 5-handle 10-year yield) have all been crossed without triggering de-escalation, and new risks (Houthi advances, a Saudi pipeline attack, Ukrainian strikes deep into Russian refineries) keep emerging with no US-Iran de-escalation signal and no guaranteed Trump-Xi breakthrough on September 24. Brent's $16 premium over JPM's $90 September fair value implies the market is pricing roughly 4 mbd of additional feared supply loss on top of 10 mbd already disrupted. Mechanically: April's Illusion of Plenty thesis expected about 1.6bn barrels of inventory draws to push and hold prices near $100. Instead actual draws totaled only 555mb, a third of that, because governments preserved barrels and let demand destruction (4.4 mbd below last year, 1.5x the inventory-implied adjustment) absorb the shock, keeping Brent's average at just $94. Remaining OECD and Chinese release capacity could still reach JPM's 7.65bn barrel stress threshold, meaning dry powder caps prices for now, though sustained disruption would still add $7-8 to 4Q26/December forecasts.
